newsitem.title: USA: United Carolina Q3 cut by loss provisions.
newsitem.headline: United Carolina Q3 cut by loss provisions.

text.p: United Carolina Bancshares Corp said Wednesday that credit loss provisions, although offset by other areas of operations, were partially behind the dip in the company's third-quarter profits.

Reporting net income of $12.05 million for the three months, down from $13.10 million in the year-ago period, Rhone Sasser, chief executive officer, said the provision for credit losses were primarily the result of "continued growth in loans, as well as costs associated with the implementation of UCB's new central computer software applications system."
"The increased credit loss provisions and operating costs were substantially offset by increased revenues from higher levels of both net interest income and noninterest income," Sasser said.
The bank also reported a 6.2-percent rise in reserves for credit losses and a 14.3-percent rise in loans charged off in the quarter.
